skill.name: context-fundamentals
skill.description: Learn how system instructions, tools, documents, message history, and outputs shape language model context and performance.
skill.summary: Design focused, efficient context for reliable language model agents.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Large, unfocused context can increase cost and reduce reliable attention. This skill teaches practical methods for selecting, organizing, loading, and compacting agent context.
actual_capabilities: Explains the roles of system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents, message history, and tool outputs.
Describes attention constraints and performance changes associated with longer context.
Applies progressive disclosure to skills, documents, and tool results.
Guides explicit context budgeting, placement, monitoring, and compaction decisions.
Provides structured examples for system prompts and staged document loading.
limitations: Provides conceptual guidance rather than automated context measurement or optimization.
Does not define model-specific token limits, pricing, or benchmark results.
Does not inspect repositories, execute commands, or modify agent configurations.
Requires environment-specific testing before applying thresholds or architecture decisions.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent Context
use_cases.description: Map each context component and decide what loads initially or on demand.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Context Failures
use_cases.description: Review an unreliable agent workflow for excessive history, noisy outputs, weak tool descriptions, or poor information placement.

use_cases.title: Teach Context Principles
use_cases.description: Create a focused introduction to context windows, attention budgets, progressive disclosure, and compaction.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Context Components
prompt_templates.prompt: List the context components in my agent design: [design]. Explain the purpose and likely token impact of each component.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing agent design

prompt_templates.title: Create a Context Budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context budget for [workflow] using a [token limit] limit. Prioritize essential information and identify content to load on demand.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Context Degradation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this agent trace for context degradation: [trace summary]. Identify attention, history, retrieval, and tool-output problems, then recommend measurable changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Progressive Context Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a progressive context architecture for [system]. Define startup context, retrieval triggers, compaction thresholds, information placement, and validation metrics with clear tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Review a support agent that loads every policy document before each conversation.
output_examples.output: Keep identity, safety rules, and policy indexes at startup. Retrieve only relevant policy sections after classifying the request.

output_examples.input: Create a context budget for an agent with a 32,000-token limit.
output_examples.output: Reserve stable space for instructions and tools, allocate bounded space for retrieved evidence, and compact history before usage approaches the selected threshold.

output_examples.input: Explain why a long agent conversation became less reliable.
output_examples.output: The growing message history and retained tool outputs diluted relevant signals. Summarize completed work, remove stale observations, and restate current constraints.

best_practices: Start with the smallest context that supports the current decision.
Place critical instructions and current goals where the model can attend to them reliably.
Measure context usage and validate compaction or retrieval changes with representative tasks.
anti_patterns: Loading all available documentation before relevance is known.
Keeping stale tool outputs and full message history throughout long workflows.
Treating a larger context window as a substitute for information selection.

faq.question: What does context include?
faq.answer: Context includes system instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, conversation history, and tool outputs available during inference.

faq.question: Does more context always improve results?
faq.answer: No. Additional tokens can increase cost and dilute attention when they are irrelevant, repetitive, or poorly organized.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: Progressive disclosure loads brief identifiers first and retrieves detailed information only when the current task requires it.

faq.question: Can this skill calculate token usage?
faq.answer: No. It provides budgeting principles but does not include a tokenizer, monitoring tool, or model-specific calculator.

faq.question: When should context be compacted?
faq.answer: Compact before history and outputs crowd out current goals, constraints, and evidence. Validate the chosen threshold for each workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill change agent files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It offers guidance and examples without reading, writing, or executing files and commands.
